extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of arithmetic (historical/abacus methods)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructional exposition on multiplication and division methods using abacus/figures, tables (tauoletta), and several historical/manual algorithms (regolo, repiego, ad andata, galea). Aimed at teaching how to perform and practice these operations and how to record intermediate parts/remainders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of division (Della Divisione)
rubrics_metrics.description: Division is making a number into as many equal parts as there are units in the divisor; to divide is to determine how many times the divisor 'enters' into the dividend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text defines division: 'Della Diuifione: Onde Diufione Del numero per altro numero fie propoffla che sieno doi numeri...' and explains one must count how many times the divisor fits into the dividend (denota d' numero de volte). Use the most significant figures first and proceed to successive figures; when parts are not integral represent them as 'rotti' (fractions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denote quotient and remainder (marking how many times)
rubrics_metrics.description: When dividing, explicitly denote how many times the divisor enters into portions of the dividend; record intermediate quotients and the remainder(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book instructs to 'Denota d numero ode volte dxl ... entra nel ...' and to write the count in the margin or in the table, bringing down further figures to continue the division. Remainders that are not integral should be treated as 'rotti' (fractional parts) and indicated with the appropriate notation (lines/marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Four principal methods of performing division (quattro modi di partire)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four main algorithms described for performing division: (1) partire a regolo / alla tauoletta / alla scritta; (2) partire per repiego; (3) partire ad andata (terzo modo); (4) partire a galea (quarto modo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates these four methods (primo, secondo, terzo, quarto) and treats each in turn, explaining when each is appropriate and giving worked examples and variations. The reader should learn all four methods to choose the most convenient depending on the problem and available materials (written table, folding/repiego technique, verbal negotiation style, or physical grouping with counters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partire a regolo / alla tauoletta / alla scritta (first method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide by arranging digits/figures on a tablet or in writing, starting from the highest-order figure and working down; mark partitions and use the table to record intermediate results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: place the figures to be divided in the table, mark the partition on the margin so you can recall it when needed, begin dividing with the first (leftmost) figure(s) and write the quotient figures; bring down subsequent figures and continue. Examples show dividing numbers like 9876 using the 'regolo' method and emphasize correct placement and not 'advancing' more parts than exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partire per repiego (second method / folding or reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Division by 'repiego' reduces numbers by successive subtractions of large multiples (folding/reducing) — choose greatest multiples (repieghi) that fit and reduce the current portion accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book explains 'partire arepiego' as selecting numbers (multiples) that form partitions (repieghi) and using them to reduce the dividend; the method involves finding a multiple that when removed leaves a remainder manageable for further division. Examples indicate choosing the largest repiego present and reapplying the process; the text links this to multiplication inversely and shows worked numeric examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partire ad andata (third method / verbal/negotiation counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A method modeled on merchants' negotiation: the operator verbally counts how many times the divisor fits into portions of the dividend (saying successive counts) and records them; suitable when many figures or when trading-style counting is natural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as the 'modo del negotiàdo', the technique consists of verbally iterating counts (e.g., 'molti, pocot, do, etc.') until the operator determines how many times the divisor enters; used especially in practical merchant computations. The text gives guidance on when to switch to more systematic written methods if ambiguity arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partire a galea (fourth method / grouping with counters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Division by 'galea' uses physical grouping (counters, tokens or objects) into piles to realize equal partitions — a material method useful for merchants and practical operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'galea' method is tied to physical 'materiale' (pieces of wood, tokens) and explained as grouping into piles until groups correspond to the divisor; the text notes its suitability when teaching or when operators have no written table, and connects the vocabulary to the material objects used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling fractional parts ('rotti') and division of non-integers
rubrics_metrics.description: When integer parts are exhausted and division continues into fractional parts, represent the fractional remainder as 'rotti' (fractions) by appropriate notation; know how to convert and continue division into rotti.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text discusses how to write rotti, where to place the figures of the fractional parts, and how to 'mettere la virgula' or line to indicate parts that aren't integral; it instructs how to treat the fractional remainder, to multiply it by further units (bringing down figures) to continue division, and gives examples of partitioning a unit into equal parts and naming them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of abacus figures and tauoletta (tables) for calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ abacus figures and prearranged tables (tauoletta) to facilitate division and multiplication; place common figures (1–9 etc.) for quick immediate division and multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: prepare a 'tauoletta' with figures and memorized multiples, place figures in table columns, and use the abacus figures as aids. The text recommends pupils learn tables (at least up to 100), keep booklets, and arrange many partitions on the tablet so the immediate division is obvious. Examples throughout show setting aside certain figures in the table and using them to find quotients quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication as repeated addition / copying figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform multiplication by repeatedly copying the group of figures that represent the multiplicand and adding them the required number of times; alignment and carrying must be managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book gives long worked-out examples (e.g., repeated application of '48' groups, sequences like 48, 96, 144, ...; many numeric strings in the OCR illustrate this practice). Guidance stresses copying the figures that represent units and adding them, using the same rule for all copies, and where necessary noting carries; it also warns that these repeated copies should be managed so as not to corrupt the figures on the tablet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking partitions, marginal notes and intermediate bookkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout division and multiplication, record partition marks, marginal notes, and intermediate lines/rules to track the process and to avoid errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual advises to place partitions at the margin or aside ('metti lo partito o a vn canto che lo scibo lo vega per ricordar se'), to use rows and lines when parts are fractional, and to re-take or re-copy figures into the table when needed. Several examples show using a margin or a separate row to note intermediate quotients so one can 'call' them back during the computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice, memorization and progressive learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery requires memorization of tables and extensive practice; operations become easier with repeated exercise and knowledge of common multiples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly tells learners to memorize at least up to 100, to practice many exercises in the tablet/books, and that what is hard at first becomes easy by practice. It also counsels teachers to provide many prepared examples and for pupils to train by repeatedly partitioning and multiplying typical figures until the methods are familiar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warnings against errors (over-advancing, wrong carrying, improper copying)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not advance more parts than the dividend allows, avoid incorrect carrying or copying that corrupts the figures, and do not lose track of the margin notes or intermediate figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual repeatedly warns 'non si può avancare più' (do not advance more), cautions about mistaken repetition and carrying, and shows examples where improper copying or failing to respect the table margins leads to wrong results. It recommends careful bookkeeping, use of the margin marks, and re-taking figures when in doubt.
